summary: Extend the existing Java URL shortener with privacy-preserving click analytics: every successful GET /{short_code} redirect records a url.clicked event via a transactional outbox (never blocking the redirect), an in-process poller publishes those events to the Kafka topic url.clicked keyed by short_code, an analytics consumer aggregates them into click_stats, and a new additive endpoint GET /api/v1/urls/{short_code}/stats exposes total clicks, last clicked timestamp, and a 30-day daily breakdown with an as_of timestamp. Raw IPs are never persisted (salted SHA-256 only), raw click events are retained 90 days, and publishing/consuming use bounded retries with exponential backoff + jitter, timeouts, and idempotency keys. The existing redirect contract stays backward compatible with no more than a 5% p95 latency increase.

stories.i_want: every successful redirect of my short link to be recorded as a click event
stories.so_that: I can see how often my link is used

stories.as_a: end user following a short link
stories.i_want: the redirect to complete at the same speed even when Kafka is slow or unavailable
stories.so_that: analytics never degrades my browsing experience

stories.i_want: an API that returns aggregated click statistics for a short code
stories.so_that: I can review total clicks, the last click time, and daily trends

stories.i_want: IP addresses to be stored only as salted SHA-256 hashes and raw events purged after 90 days
stories.so_that: the service stays compliant with privacy and retention policy

stories.i_want: outbox publishing and consumption to use bounded retries with exponential backoff, jitter, timeouts, and idempotency keys
stories.so_that: transient broker or database failures do not cause data loss, duplicates, or unbounded resource use

stories.i_want: the current redirect and URL endpoints to keep their exact contract
stories.so_that: my integration continues to work after the analytics release

acceptance_criteria.given: a short code that resolves to a target URL
acceptance_criteria.when: a client issues GET /{short_code} and the service returns a successful redirect response
acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one row is committed to the outbox table in the same database transaction as the redirect handling, containing short_code, occurred_at (UTC), hashed_ip, referrer_host and an idempotency key

acceptance_criteria.given: a request for an unknown or expired short code
acceptance_criteria.when: GET /{short_code} does not produce a successful redirect
acceptance_criteria.then: no outbox row and no url.clicked event are created

acceptance_criteria.given: Kafka is unreachable or responding slower than the configured timeout
acceptance_criteria.then: the redirect response is returned with its normal status and Location header, the request does not block on any Kafka call, and the event remains pending in the outbox for later publication

acceptance_criteria.given: pending rows exist in the outbox table
acceptance_criteria.then: it claims a bounded batch using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, publishes each event to topic url.clicked with short_code as the message key, and marks published rows so they are not published again by a concurrent poller instance

acceptance_criteria.given: the Kafka producer or consumer call fails with a transient error
acceptance_criteria.then: attempts are retried with exponential backoff plus jitter up to the configured maximum attempts, each attempt bounded by a timeout, and after exhaustion the event is left in a terminal/failed state that is logged and metered rather than retried forever

acceptance_criteria.given: the same url.clicked event (same idempotency key) is delivered to the analytics consumer more than once
acceptance_criteria.then: click_stats totals, last_clicked_at and clicks_by_day reflect the event exactly once

acceptance_criteria.given: url.clicked events have been consumed for a short code
acceptance_criteria.then: click_stats holds short_code, total_clicks, last_clicked_at and clicks_by_day where day buckets are computed in UTC

acceptance_criteria.given: a short code that exists and has recorded clicks
acceptance_criteria.when: a client calls GET /api/v1/urls/{short_code}/stats with credentials accepted by the existing /api/v1 auth scheme
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 200 with total_clicks, last_clicked_at, an as_of timestamp, and clicks_by_day as an ordered list of {date, count} covering the last 30 days

acceptance_criteria.given: a short code that does not exist
a redirect request carrying a client IP address
acceptance_criteria.when: the click event is persisted and published
acceptance_criteria.then: the payload contains only the SHA-256 hash of the IP combined with the configured static salt, and no raw IP value appears in the outbox table, click_stats, Kafka payloads or application logs

acceptance_criteria.given: a redirect request with a Referer header
acceptance_criteria.then: referrer_host contains only the host component with no path or query, and is null when the header is absent or cannot be parsed as a URI

acceptance_criteria.given: raw click event rows older than 90 days
acceptance_criteria.then: those raw rows are deleted while click_stats aggregate rows remain unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: the baseline redirect latency measured before the change
acceptance_criteria.when: the automated load-test gate runs against the build with analytics enabled
acceptance_criteria.then: p95 latency of GET /{short_code} is no more than 5% above baseline and the gate fails the build otherwise

acceptance_criteria.given: existing clients of GET /{short_code} and the current /api/v1 URL endpoints
acceptance_criteria.then: existing request/response contracts are unchanged, only additive fields and the new stats endpoint are introduced, and the existing contract test suite passes unmodified

acceptance_criteria.given: a click event published but not yet consumed
acceptance_criteria.then: the response reflects eventual consistency and its as_of timestamp indicates the point in time the aggregate was last updated

non_goals: Bot, crawler or fraud filtering of clicks
Analytics on unsuccessful redirect attempts (404s, expired links)
Salt rotation or re-hashing of historical hashed_ip values
Geo-IP, device, browser or user-agent enrichment
A dashboard, UI or CSV/report export for click statistics
Provisioning or configuring the Kafka cluster and the url.clicked topic (owned by infrastructure)
Real-time/strongly consistent stats or streaming push of click updates
Deleting or expiring click_stats aggregate rows

ambiguities.question: What retry bounds should the outbox publisher and analytics consumer use (max attempts and backoff ceiling)?
options: Configurable via application properties with documented defaults
ambiguities.default_if_unanswered: Configurable via application properties with defaults of 5 attempts, base 100ms, cap 10s, full jitter

ambiguities.question: Where should the analytics consumer store click_stats?
options: Same relational database/schema as the shortener
Separate schema in the same database instance
ambiguities.default_if_unanswered: Same relational database as the shortener, in a separate table owned by the analytics module

ambiguities.question: What should GET /api/v1/urls/{short_code}/stats return for a short code that exists but has zero recorded clicks?
options: 200 with total_clicks=0, last_clicked_at=null and 30 zero-count day entries
200 with total_clicks=0, last_clicked_at=null and an empty clicks_by_day list
ambiguities.default_if_unanswered: 200 with total_clicks=0, last_clicked_at=null and an empty clicks_by_day list

ambiguities.question: Should clicks_by_day include days with zero clicks within the 30-day window?
options: Yes, dense list with zero-filled days
No, sparse list containing only days with at least one click
ambiguities.default_if_unanswered: No, sparse list containing only days with at least one click

ambiguities.question: How should the 90-day raw click event purge be triggered?
options: In-process scheduled job in the application
Database-level partition drop / scheduled SQL job
External infrastructure cron outside the service
ambiguities.default_if_unanswered: In-process scheduled job in the application, with interval and batch size configurable

ambiguities.question: What scope defines the idempotency key for a click event?
options: Random UUID generated per redirect and carried end-to-end
Deterministic hash of (short_code, occurred_at, hashed_ip, referrer_host)
Outbox row primary key / monotonic sequence id
ambiguities.default_if_unanswered: Random UUID generated per redirect, stored on the outbox row and carried in the Kafka message header

ambiguities.question: What poller cadence and batch size should the outbox publisher use?
ambiguities.default_if_unanswered: Configurable with defaults of 500ms interval and batch size 100

assumptions: hashed_ip is computed with SHA-256 over a single static salt read from the existing secret/config mechanism; the salt is never rotated (AMB-1).
Outbox draining is performed by an in-process scheduled poller using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED batching, safe for multiple application instances (AMB-2).
clicks_by_day covers the last 30 days and is returned as an ordered list of {date, count} objects (AMB-3).
All timestamps and day bucketing use UTC (AMB-4).
The 90-day retention applies to raw click events only; click_stats aggregates are retained indefinitely (AMB-5).
The latency budget is a maximum 5% p95 increase on GET /{short_code}, verified by an automated load-test gate in CI (AMB-6).
The new stats endpoint reuses whatever authentication/authorization scheme the existing /api/v1 endpoints already enforce (AMB-7).
referrer_host holds the host component only (no path or query) and is null when the Referer header is absent or unparsable (AMB-8).
Stats are eventually consistent and the response includes an as_of timestamp (AMB-9).
The Kafka topic url.clicked is provisioned by infrastructure; messages are keyed by short_code to preserve per-code ordering (AMB-10).
Only successful redirects generate click events; no bot filtering is performed (AMB-11).
The work is brownfield: it extends the existing Java URL shortener in the workspace and reuses its current persistence, configuration and build tooling.
